sentences.text:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Mr.S.A.Mohta counsel for the applicant.
 Mr.V.P.Maldhure, App counsel for the respondent.

Coram : Manish Pitale, J.
Date : 12.06.2019.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant.

2. Issue notice, returnable on 10th July, 2019.
3. Learned APP Mr. V.P.Maldhure waives notice on behalf of the respondent/State.

4. The applicant is one of the accused in First Information Report dated 1.6.2019 registered against him and two other persons for allegedly having committed offences under Sections 188, 272, 328 r/w Sec.34 of the Indian Penal Code r/w Sec.26(2)(i), 26(2)(iv), 27(3)(b)(e), 59 of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006.
It is alleged that the co-accused persons were intercepted and found to be in possession of huge quantity of Guthkha, which is a prohibited item in the state of Maharashtra.

It is alleged that said material recovered from the co- accused was found to be worth Rs. 1,884,400.00/-
KAVITA 1-aba-351-19.odt and when enquiry was made with the co-accused they took name of the applicant as a person to whom the material belonged.
On this basis, First Information Report was registered against all the accused persons including the applicant herein.

1 5.

The learned counsel appearing for the applicant points out that Section 328 of the Indian Penal Code would not apply in the present case at all, because the ingredients of the said offence are not made out in the present case.
Reliance is placed by the learned counsel for the applicant on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Joseph Kurian..
Vrs..State of Kerala reported in (1994)6 SCC 535.

It is contended that the other offences are also not made out against the applicant and that other than the statement of the co-accused there appears nothing to connect the applicant with the alleged offence.
6. In view of the aforesaid material available before the Court at present, the applicant has made out the case for grant of ad interim protection.

The learned APP has opposed grant of such ad interim protection, contending that the judgment of Devision Bench of this Court covers the case against the applicant insofar as section 328 of the Indian Penal Code is concerned and it is further contended that custody of the applicant would be required to KAVITA 1-aba-351-19.odt enquire about the syndicate behind the manufacture, supply and transport of the aforesaid prohibited material.
7. In these circumstances, ad interim protection can be granted to the applicant.

Hence in the event,
the applicant is arrested in Crime No.170 of 2019 registered at police station Murtizapur rural, dist.
Akola, he shall be released on bail on furnishing the PR bond of Rs.50,000/- with surety in the like amount.
The applicant shall co-
operate with the investigation.
He shall remain present before the Investigating officer on 14th June 2019 at 10.00 a.m. and on further such occasions as the Investigating officer may direct.
8. The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence or influence the witnesses.
9. The learned counsel for the applicant seeks leave to make correction in the index and list of annexures.
10. Leave is granted .
11. The correction/amendment be carried out forthwith.
12. Hamdast is granted.
